'source' is how that update was recorded: "user" means the user explicitly stated or corrected it; "inference" means the agent inferred or guessed it; "observation" means the agent observed it indirectly. Resolve each conflict using whatever signal actually distinguishes the two updates — e.g. a user-sourced, higher-confidence update is ordinarily more trustworthy than an inferred, lower-confidence one; the ancestor value can indicate which branch's update is more likely a genuine correction vs. a stale duplicate. If source, confidence, and ancestor context give no real basis to prefer one branch over the other (e.g. both are equally plausible, equally-sourced preference changes), explicitly flag it as unresolvable rather than guessing.
